cards.front: Recall a key point about The League in the 1930s
cards.back: On 18 September 1931, Japan used the "Mukden Incident" - an explosion on the Japanese-owned South Manchurian Railway - as a pretext to invade Manchuria, a region of northern China. Japan occupied the entire province and set up the puppet state of "Manchukuo" in February 1932. The League's response was slow, weak, and ultimately ineffective.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The League in the 1930s
cards.back: In October 1935, Italy invaded Abyssinia (modern Ethiopia), one of the few independent African nations. The League imposed economic sanctions on Italy but they were half-hearted and failed to stop the invasion. By May 1936, Italy had conquered Abyssinia. The crisis was the League's most humiliating failure and effectively destroyed it as a peacekeeping body.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The League in the 1930s
cards.back: The Great Depression that followed the 1929 Wall Street Crash fundamentally changed the international environment. Economic crisis made nations more aggressive, more self-interested, and less willing to cooperate through the League.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The League in the 1930s
cards.back: The World Disarmament Conference opened in Geneva on 2 February 1932 with 60 nations represented. It was the League's most ambitious attempt to reduce armaments. After nearly 18 months of negotiation, it collapsed completely in June 1934 without achieving any significant agreement.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The League in the 1930s
cards.back: By 1936, collective security was effectively dead. The League had failed to stop Japan in Manchuria, failed to stop Italy in Abyssinia, and failed to achieve disarmament. When Hitler remilitarised the Rhineland in March 1936, no one even asked the League to act. The League continued to exist technically until 1946, but as a peacekeeping body it was finished by 1936.

cards.front: What should you know about history exam tips — the league in the 1930s?
cards.back: 1. For The League in the 1930s, include specific factual detail: dates, names, events and statistics where relevant 2. For source questions, analyse provenance (who, when, why, audience) before using the content 3. In evaluation questions, discuss multiple factors and weigh their relative significance 4. Always link back to the question focus — don't just narrate what happened with The League in the 1930s 5. Use phrases like 'the most significant factor was... because...' to show analytical judgement
